common_name: Desert Blaze Autumn Sage (Variegated Gold-Leaf Salvia greggii)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained to dry, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun; strong light keeps the leaf variegation vivid.

directions: Desert Blaze is a Salvia greggii selection grown chiefly for its foliage, each leaf broadly edged in creamy gold around a green center, topped from spring through fall with the same small two-lipped red flowers typical of autumn sage. The variegation is most pronounced in full sun and tends to green up in shade, and the plant grows a bit more slowly than solid-green greggii selections. It is a dependable hummingbird plant and pairs well with purple- or blue-flowered companions that set off the bright foliage. Cut back hard in late winter to renew dense, well-colored new growth.

common_name: Navajo Bright Pink Autumn Sage (Vivid Pink Salvia greggii, Navajo Series)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained to dry, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun.

directions: Navajo Bright Pink is a member of the Navajo series of Salvia greggii selections, covering its tidy, rounded form in saturated hot-pink, two-lipped flowers that read more vivid than the softer magenta-rose of 'Navajo Rose'. It blooms in continuous flushes from spring through hard frost and is a steady hummingbird and native bee draw through the growing season. Like other Navajo series selections it is highly drought- and heat-tolerant once established, needing only occasional deep watering on lean, well-drained soil. Cut back hard to 6-8 inches in late winter to renew dense growth and maximize the following season's bloom.

common_name: Sierra San Antonio Sage (Pale Yellow Salvia x jamensis)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun; excellent drainage is essential to avoid floppy, short-lived growth.

directions: Sierra San Antonio is a Salvia x jamensis selection traced to wild collections from a mountain range in northeastern Mexico, valued for pale creamy-yellow flowers that are unusual among the reds, pinks, and purples typical of greggii-microphylla hybrids. It forms a compact, mounding, well-branched shrub that blooms from late spring into fall and draws hummingbirds and bees throughout the season. Light trimming after each bloom flush keeps the plant tidy and encourages fresh flowering; it is extremely drought-tolerant once established and well suited to rock gardens and containers.

common_name: Jezebel Salvia (Deep Wine-Red Salvia x jamensis)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun.

directions: Jezebel is an English-raised Salvia x jamensis hybrid prized for deep wine-red to burgundy, two-lipped flowers on a compact, well-branched, aromatic shrub blooming from late spring into fall. The rich, dark flower color stands out against the grayish-green foliage and draws hummingbirds and bees steadily through the long bloom season. It shares the excellent drought tolerance of its greggii and microphylla parents, needing minimal supplemental water once established on lean, sharply drained soil. Trim lightly after each flush to keep growth dense and encourage continued flowering.

common_name: Pat Vlasto Salvia (Soft Pink Salvia x jamensis)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun.

directions: Pat Vlasto is an English-raised Salvia x jamensis hybrid bearing soft, clear pink, two-lipped flowers on a compact, rounded, aromatic shrub from late spring through fall. Its gentle pastel color works well in mixed borders alongside the more saturated reds and purples common among other jamensis and greggii selections. Like its parent species it is highly drought-tolerant once established, needing little supplemental water on lean, well-drained soil, and it draws hummingbirds and bees throughout its long bloom season. Shear lightly after each flush to maintain a tidy, floriferous shape.

common_name: Peter Vidgeon Salvia (Rose-Pink Salvia x jamensis)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun.

directions: Peter Vidgeon is an English-raised Salvia x jamensis hybrid producing rose-pink, two-lipped flowers in continuous flushes from late spring through fall on a compact, well-branched, aromatic shrub. It is a reliable hummingbird and bee plant wherever it is grown and, like other jamensis hybrids, is exceptionally drought-tolerant once established on lean, sharply drained soil. Give it full sun and avoid overly rich or consistently moist conditions, which produce looser, less floriferous growth. Trim lightly after each bloom flush to keep the plant dense and encourage reflushing.

common_name: Pleasant View Baby Sage (Deep Red Salvia microphylla)

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in late summer or set out container plants in spring, in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun.

directions: Pleasant View is an English-raised Salvia microphylla selection forming a bushy, well-branched mound of aromatic foliage topped with deep red, two-lipped flowers from summer into fall. It is a strong hummingbird and bee plant through its long bloom season and tolerates heat and drought well once established, needing supplemental water only during extended dry spells. Cut back hard to 6-12 inches in late winter to renew growth and keep the plant dense and floriferous for the following season.

common_name: Nachtvlinder Baby Sage (Dark Maroon-Black Salvia microphylla)

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in late summer or set out container plants in spring, in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun.

directions: Nachtvlinder, Dutch for 'night moth', is a Salvia microphylla selection named for its unusually dark maroon-black flowers, among the darkest found in the genus, held above aromatic green foliage on an upright, well-branched shrub from summer into fall. The near-black flower color makes it a distinctive accent against the reds, pinks, and purples typical of other microphylla cultivars, and it remains a reliable draw for hummingbirds and bees. Cut back hard to 6-12 inches in late winter to renew growth and keep the plant dense; established plants tolerate heat and drought well.

common_name: Dientes de Dragon Baby Sage (Large-Flowered Bicolor Salvia microphylla)

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in late summer or set out container plants in spring, in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun.

directions: Dientes de Dragon, Spanish for 'dragon's teeth', is a wild-collected Salvia microphylla form from Mexico noted for flowers distinctly larger than typical microphylla cultivars, colored in a bold red-and-white bicolor pattern. It forms a vigorous, wide-spreading mound of aromatic foliage and blooms from summer into fall, drawing hummingbirds readily to its oversized flowers. Established plants tolerate heat and drought well, needing only occasional deep watering, and benefit from a hard cutback to 6-12 inches in late winter to renew dense growth.
